subject: Leadership recap: outcomes, procurement path, and escalation lanes for Zephyrus
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@zephyrusai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Leadership recap: outcomes, procurement path, and escalation lanes for Zephyrus

Daniel — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our leadership-level discussion and proposed next steps so your execs have a concise artifact. Please flag anything I missed or that you want reworded for your board.

Call summary (top-line)
- Business outcome: Reduce customer LLM inference cost per transaction by ~40% while keeping P95 latency under 300ms for priority workflows (billing approval flow, customer search).
- Success metric: Pilot target = 40% cost reduction on quantifiable token throughput for the billing pipeline within 8 weeks.
- Risk tolerance: Zephyrus wants isolation for PHI-adjacent logs and auditability; they require SOC2-type controls and evidence for audit readiness.

Key pain points you emphasized
- Spiky monthly batch runs create large cost variance and unpredictable tail latency.
- Existing vendor lacks transparent cost attribution and token-level traceability for chargebacks.
- Procurement/legal need a clear procurement path with an option to start with a low-risk pilot before committing to a yearly reserved contract.

Proposed procurement path (recommended)
1) Pilot (6–8 weeks): Hosted Redwood with a dedicated pilot pool + prefix caching for the billing workflow. Measured deliverables: cost per token delta, P95 latency, error rate baseline.
2) Security review (parallel): provide security-matrix + SOC2 artifacts; Redwood assigns an engineer for evidence collection.
3) Commercial: post-pilot exec readout -> optional Dedicated capacity commit or Private deployment discussion.

Open escalation items (what I promised to resolve by our next checkpoint)
- Provide a redlined pilot SOW and a statement of work stub for your procurement team (attached).
- Confirm which logs/data streams Zephyrus will classify as PHI-adjacent so we can scope retention and KMS requirements.
- Share timing for your internal procurement & legal review (Maya / procurement@zephyrusai.com).

Attachments: redwood_exec_recap_zephyrus_20260905.pdf (this recap), sow-draft-v1.pdf (pilot SOW draft), security-matrix.xlsx (SOC2 artifacts overview).

Next steps
- I will introduce Marissa (sales ops) and Jonas (solutions) to streamline procurement and technical onboarding.
- You to confirm procurement contact and preferred pilot start window (we suggested Sep 21 – Oct 1).
- Brief technical kickoff and access checklist once procurement signals go-ahead.

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the formal SOW and a one-page pilot success criteria doc by EOD tomorrow.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
redwood.ai
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@zephyrusai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Cheng <maya.cheng@zephyrusai.com>, procurement@zephyrusai.com
Date: 2026-09-05T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership recap: outcomes, procurement path, and escalation lanes for Zephyrus

Sofia — thanks for the thorough note. This captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot scope: good to keep billing approval flow as priority. Please add the customer-search reranker as a secondary workload in the SOW so we can measure cross-workload behavior.
- PHI-adjacent data: we will provide a named list tomorrow; for now assume invoice metadata + partial payment notes are in scope.
- Procurement timing: Maya is copied — we aim to have a procurement/ legal sync the week of Sep 14. Procurement contact is procurement@zephyrusai.com.

Two asks for your team: 
1) Can you include a simple rollback/fallback plan in the SOW in case latency regressions appear during pilot?
2) Please surface any third-party dependencies or infra requirements for a private deployment path (we may need an internal architectural review).

I'll take a look at the pilot SOW you attach and loop in our CTO if needed after Maya reviews.

—
Daniel Park
CTO, Zephyrus AI
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@zephyrusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Maya Cheng <maya.cheng@zephyrusai.com>, procurement@zephyrusai.com
Date: 2026-09-06T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Leadership recap: outcomes, procurement path, and escalation lanes for Zephyrus

Thanks Daniel — noted and added. Attaching the SOW draft and a one-pager on rollback/fallback controls. Highlights of what we added based on your asks: 

- Pilot SOW: primary workload = billing approval flow; secondary = customer-search reranker. Pilot acceptance criteria include cost reduction threshold and P95 latency target; we added an explicit rollback trigger (3% drop in acceptance score or 2x increase in error rate over baseline).
- Rollback/fallback: we included an automatic fallback policy to your incumbent endpoint for any request that exceeds 500ms or fails the inference health checks; policy is configurable per-route.
- Infra dependencies: private deployment path notes include required VPC peering, optional HSM/KMS integration details, and a brief list of supported GPU instance families (for your architect team).

Action items (owners & rough dates)
- Marissa: finalize SOW commercial terms and send an initial quote by Sep 10.
- Sofia: deliver final one-pager on pilot success criteria and evidence pack by Sep 6 EOD (attached).
- Maya / Procurement: confirm legal review window (requested Sep 14–18).
- Jonas: prepare a 30-min technical kickoff agenda and an onboarding checklist for infra access (target Sep 21).

Attachments included (3): sow-draft-v1.pdf, security-matrix.xlsx, redwood_exec_recap_zephyrus_20260905.pdf

Let me know if you'd like this doc rephrased for your board and I can produce a 1-slide summary.

Best,

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zephyrusai.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Leadership recap: outcomes, procurement path, and escalation lanes for Zephyrus

Looping Marissa on the procurement ask — I reviewed the SOW and pilot acceptance language; two quick technical clarifications we should include before sending to Zephyrus procurement: 

- Include explicit latency SLA target for the pilot (P95 <= 300ms) and how we measure it (internal tracing + request sampling).
- Note that KV cache warm-up may affect first-week cost measurements; recommend a 5-day stability window for cost comparisons.

Marissa — can you add these to the commercial SOW and propose the quote band? I can draft a short paragraph for the technical appendix.

Thanks,
Jonas
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
